title: NGC 602 (NIRCam and MIRI image)
caption: The young star cluster NGC 602, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 602 · constellation Hydrus · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, P. Zeidler, E. Sabbi, A. Nota, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb)

recognition.text: Ranked #2 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A star cluster sits inside a large, many-coloured nebula of gas and dust. Dark ridges and peaks surround it, lit on their inner sides, with thin, translucent clouds draped over them. All around, a huge number of distant galaxies shine through, along with a few large, bright foreground stars. This is NGC 602, a young cluster on the fringes of the Small Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy about 200 000 light-years away.

Its surroundings resemble conditions in the early Universe, with very few elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Dark clouds of dense dust and plenty of ionised gas suggest that stars are still forming, so the cluster offers a chance to study star birth under conditions very different from those near the Sun.
Using Webb, a team including Peter Zeidler, Elena Sabbi and Antonella Nota found candidates for the first young brown dwarfs detected outside our Milky Way.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.43 x 2.90 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 258 × 169 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Webb's NIRCam and MIRI. The shortest wavelengths, 1.15 to 1.5 micrometres, are shown in blue, followed by 2.1 in cyan, 2.77 in green, 3.35 in yellow, 3.56 in orange, and 4.8 and 10 micrometres in red.
understand.eye: All of this is infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the faint brown dwarfs would never be visible without Webb.

explore: Brown dwarfs are objects too small to sustain nuclear fusion in their cores like true stars, which makes young ones faint and hard to find at such distances.
alt: A star cluster inside a colourful nebula with dark, lit-edged ridges and translucent clouds, surrounded by many distant galaxies and a few bright foreground stars.
